subject.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose this broad flat cron add/update interface—including provider and tool-policy-related fields—in the generic model-facing cron tool schema despite its prompt-cost and compatibility footprint?
rationale: The implementation is internally guarded and proof-backed, but choosing which cron controls belong in the model-facing contract is an owner policy decision rather than a mechanical correction.

options.title: Approve the bounded flat contract
options.body: Accept the tested flat add/update interface as a supported model-facing cron API and own its prompt-budget and compatibility surface.

options.title: Narrow the advertised fields
options.body: Keep only the minimal fields needed for the reported malformed add/update flows and leave sensitive or rarely used controls nested until separately approved.

options.title: Pause for a cron API design pass
options.body: Defer this PR until owners define the long-term flat-versus-nested cron tool contract alongside the remaining payload-field work.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded flat contract
recommendation.body: Accept the tested flat add/update interface as a supported model-facing cron API and own its prompt-budget and compatibility surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged cron compatibility work is the closest demonstrated ownership signal for the schema and payload contract affected by this decision.
